subject: Polity
description: Articles 5-11, Citizenship Act 1955, OCI/PIO, NRC, CAA 2019

questions.stem: Indian citizenship by Constitution is dealt with under:
questions.explanation: Part II — Articles 5-11. Art 5 — citizens at commencement of Constitution (those domiciled or born in India + parents born in India + 5-yr ordinary residents). Art 6 — migrants from Pakistan. Art 7 — those who migrated TO Pakistan. Art 8 — Indians abroad. Art 9 — voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship → Indian citizenship lost. Art 10 — continuance of citizenship. Art 11 — Parliament's power to legislate (resulted in Citizenship Act 1955). India follows JUS SANGUINIS (parental ancestry) primarily, with limited JUS SOLI (birth on territory).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Citizenship Act, 1955' provides for FIVE modes of acquisition. Which of these is NOT one?

options.option_text: Marriage to an Indian citizen automatically

questions.explanation: Five modes — Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation of territory. Marriage does NOT automatically confer citizenship; spouse can REGISTER after 7 years of marriage + ordinary residence. India does NOT permit dual citizenship. PIO/OCI cards (Persons of Indian Origin / Overseas Citizen of India) — confer some rights (no visa, multiple-entry, work) but not voting / political rights / agricultural land purchase. PIO scheme merged into OCI in 2015.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CAA 2019 (Citizenship Amendment Act) provided expedited naturalisation for non-Muslim refugees from:

options.option_text: Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan — for Hindus, Sikhs, Christians, Parsis, Jains, Buddhists who entered before 31 December 2014

questions.explanation: CAA 2019 (in force March 2024 with rules notified) — eased naturalisation for SIX persecuted minority communities (Hindus, Sikhs, Christians, Parsis, Jains, Buddhists) from Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan who entered India before 31 December 2014. Reduced naturalisation period from 11 years to 6 years. Excluded MUSLIMS — major controversy. Critics argued violates Article 14 (Right to Equality). Sparked nationwide protests + Shaheen Bagh sit-in. Constitutional challenges pending in Supreme Court. NRC + CAA seen by many as combined exercise.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'OCI' (Overseas Citizen of India) status is essentially:

options.option_text: A lifelong visa giving most rights of NRIs except voting, agricultural-land purchase, and political/government office

questions.explanation: OCI — introduced 2005. Eligible: foreign citizens who were Indian citizens or whose parents/grandparents were Indian. NOT eligible: Pakistan, Bangladesh nationals (or those whose ancestors were). OCI rights: lifelong visa, no police registration, can work + invest + buy non-agricultural property in India. NOT entitled to: vote, contest elections, hold government posts (President, MPs, judges, IAS), buy agricultural land. India does NOT permit dual citizenship in the strict sense — OCI is a lifelong visa. Renunciation: must give up OCI within 6 months of acquiring Indian citizenship.

questions.stem: The NRC (National Register of Citizens) — first updated 2019 in which state?

options.option_text: Assam — final NRC published 31 August 2019; ~19 lakh excluded

questions.explanation: NRC Assam — updated 31 August 2019 under SC monitoring. Final list — 3.30 crore included, ~19 lakh excluded. Excluded persons can appeal to Foreigners' Tribunals. NRC originated from Assam Accord (1985) — cut-off date 24 March 1971 (one day before Bangladesh War). Government has indicated nationwide NRC discussion (no implementation yet); States like West Bengal, Kerala, Punjab, Rajasthan have passed assembly resolutions against. NPR (National Population Register) — every-resident exercise updated 2010, 2015, scheduled 2024-25 (delayed), distinct from NRC.

questions.stem: An Indian citizen who voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship:

options.option_text: Loses Indian citizenship immediately (Art 9 + Sec 9 of Citizenship Act)
Can hold both at the same time as 'dual citizen'

questions.explanation: Article 9 + Section 9 of Citizenship Act, 1955 — voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship → automatic termination of Indian citizenship. India does NOT recognise dual citizenship (strict reading; OCI is technically a lifelong visa, not citizenship). Surrender of Indian passport mandatory; failing — penal provisions. Some countries (USA, UK, Canada) permit dual; India does not. PIO+OCI merger 2015. To regain Indian citizenship after losing, must apply for naturalisation (12 of last 14 years residence + 1 year continuous before application).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.explanation: INDIA — single citizenship (despite federal structure, citizenship is Indian — borrowed from UK). USA — dual citizenship (federal + state). Single citizenship promotes national integration and uniform rights. Articles 5-11 codify; Citizenship Act 1955 implements. Special UTs / states may have additional residence rules — Jammu & Kashmir's previous Article 35A (revoked August 2019 along with Art 370 abrogation) had limited 'permanent resident' status; now defunct.
